name: Scatter-Gather
intent: Send one request to many workers at the same time, then collect and combine their answers within a time limit.
scenario: A price-comparison page asks five vendors for a price. Each answers at its own speed, and one is slow and one is broken.
problem: The page asks the vendors one after another, so the waiting times add up, and a single slow vendor holds up the whole page. If one fails, the page may fail with it.
solution: A scatterer sends the request to all five vendors at once. A gatherer collects the answers as they arrive, until all are in or a deadline passes. It ignores workers that are too slow or fail, merges what it has (here, the best price) and says how many answers it used. The page takes as long as the slowest answer it is willing to wait for, not the sum of all of them.
pain: The waiting times of all vendors are added together
One slow vendor makes every page slow
One failing vendor can break the whole page
Nobody decides how long is too long to wait
benefits: Total time is about the slowest answer you accept, not the sum
A deadline puts a limit on the wait
A slow or failed worker costs one answer, not the whole page
Adding a vendor raises the waiting time only if it is slower than the rest, and never past the deadline
whenToUse: One request needs answers from many independent sources, such as vendors or shards
A partial answer is acceptable when some sources are slow
The sources do not depend on each other's answers
whenNotToUse: A step needs the previous step's answer: it cannot run in parallel
The answer is only correct if every source replies, such as an exact total
When fanning out would overload a source that is already struggling
pitfalls: Without a deadline, the gather step waits for the slowest worker, however slow
A partial result passed off as a complete one misleads users: say how many answers were used
Fanning out to many workers multiplies load, and one slow worker still ties up resources
Merging results needs rules, such as ordering, duplicates and ties

roles.label: Caller
roles.description: Asks one question and wants one combined answer.

roles.label: Scatterer
roles.description: Sends the request to every worker at the same time.

roles.label: Worker
roles.description: A vendor or shard that answers on its own, or fails, or is too slow.

roles.label: Gatherer
roles.description: Collects answers until all arrive or the deadline passes, then combines them.

quiz.question: A comparison page asks five vendors one after another, each taking about 150 ms, so the page takes about 750 ms. What is the best change?
options: Cache the five answers for an hour so that most visitors never wait for the vendors
Ask only the two fastest vendors so that the page shows results sooner
Send the request to all five at once and combine the answers when they arrive
Ask for fewer fields from each vendor, so that each answer is a little bit smaller
quiz.explanation: The vendors do not depend on each other, so they can be asked in parallel, and the page takes about as long as the slowest one, around 150 ms. Caching shows stale prices, dropping vendors loses offers, and smaller answers hardly change the waiting time.

quiz.question: With parallel calls, the page still takes 5 seconds whenever one vendor is slow. Four answers are in after 200 ms. What should the gatherer do?
options: Wait until a deadline such as 300 ms, then return the answers that have arrived, marked as partial
Wait for the slow vendor, because a page without all five vendors is not correct
Send the request again to the slow vendor and wait for whichever answer comes first
Return an error to the user until all five vendors can answer within the time limit
quiz.explanation: For a price comparison, four prices now are better than five prices in five seconds. A deadline caps the wait, and saying that the result is partial keeps the page honest. Waiting for everyone or returning an error makes one vendor decide the speed for all. Re-sending to the same slow vendor doubles its load and still leaves the page waiting on it.

quiz.question: A service uses scatter-gather over 10 database shards to compute an account's exact total, and one shard times out. What is the best behaviour?
options: Add up the nine answers that arrived and show that as the total, as it is the best available
Ignore the failing shard for ever, and never ask it again until the next restart
Return the total as zero, so that the user knows that something went wrong with the shard
Treat it as a failure or retry, because an exact total cannot be built from a partial answer
quiz.explanation: Whether a partial answer is acceptable depends on the use. A price list can be partial. An exact total cannot, so a missing shard must fail or be retried, and not be shown as complete. Zero and silent skipping are wrong answers that look right.
